preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(x) < 32768 for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: All input integers a_i satisfy 0 ≤ a_i < 32768, where stdin is the full input text and the first integer is n (1 ≤ n ≤ 32768).

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split()) == n and stdout.split()[i] == str(min_operations(int(stdin.split()[i+1]))) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each a_i in the input, the i-th output integer is the minimum number of operations (increment or multiply-by-2 modulo 32768) required to reduce a_i to 0. The output is a space-separated list of these integers.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(x) <= 100000 for x in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a non-negative integer representing a feasible operation count (no more than 100,000 operations are needed for any a_i < 32768).
